notes: The head of `אַחֲרִית` → *the latter end* is the one genuinely open point. Rule 31's tie-break arguably favours *end*, since the ASV writes a bare *end* for `אַחֲרִית` elsewhere, which would make it the class noun and *latter* the specifier; the accepted head on *latter* reads *end* as the supplied generic. Both readings are defensible and the unit already names the competing one, so it is left as accepted rather than overturned on a head choice.
`אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר` fused to the single *fourteen* (rule 30), headed on the governing first morpheme.
`הָיָה` takes the *had*, its `לְ` is `unrepresented`, and the suffix takes the subject *he* (rules 40, 43).
